messages:
yuki: hey team, new hire here. following the README on Windows + WSL2. started postgres with docker-compose but `psql` on Windows client keeps saying "could not connect to server: No such file or directory". compose maps 5432:5432. any Windows-specific gotchas?

marcos: welcome! that error means psql is trying to use a unix domain socket (the file) not TCP. On Windows the native psql client may prefer a socket path that doesn't exist. Try `psql -h localhost -p 5432` to force TCP.

yuki: `psql -h localhost` gives connection refused. in WSL2 I can `psql -h localhost` and it works, but Windows terminal fails.

anya: WSL2 runs a lightweight VM so localhost inside WSL and host Windows localhost are different. Docker Desktop uses a VM too. For Windows apps, use host.docker.internal to reach services published by Docker Desktop: `psql -h host.docker.internal -p 5432`. In WSL you can use `localhost` if the client runs inside WSL.

marcos: also on Windows check Windows Defender / firewall blocking. If `nc -vz host.docker.internal 5432` from Windows CMD/PowerShell times out, allow Docker Desktop in firewall.

yuki: tried `psql -h host.docker.internal` from Windows and it connects! thanks. follow-up: is it safe to set DATABASE_URL to host.docker.internal in .env for the repo? might confuse mac/linux users.

anya: don't commit host.docker.internal as a default. Typical pattern: use compose service name `db` for container-to-container comms and set `DATABASE_URL` in your local override `.env.local` depending on your environment. We have a helper script `scripts/start-local.sh` in repo that writes the right host for Windows vs WSL. Check the onboarding notes.

marcos: if you want a cross-platform env var, some teams use `DB_HOST=${DB_HOST:-db}` in `.env.example`, then devs set DB_HOST=host.docker.internal locally on Windows. Keep `.env.example` generic.

devex-bot: pinned: Windows + WSL2 checklist: 1) client location matters (Windows vs WSL) 2) force TCP with `-h` to avoid unix sockets 3) use `host.docker.internal` from Windows to reach Docker Desktop services 4) prefer service names when services are in compose 5) document DB_HOST in `.env.example`. Internal guide: https://redwood.internal/dev/local-db-windows

yuki: great, working now. added a note to my onboarding doc and left a `.env.local.example` showing host.docker.internal for Windows. thanks all :)
